after.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-2-3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-2+3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-2+3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5+2\text{i}}{-2-3\text{i}} & =\frac{5+2\text{i}}{-2-3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-2+3\text{i}}{-2+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{(5+2\text{i})(-2+3\text{i})}{(-2)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-10+15\text{i}-4\text{i}+6{\text{i}}^{2}}{4-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{-10+11\text{i}+6(-1)}{13} \\  & =\frac{-16+11\text{i}}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-16+11\text{i}}{13}=(-\frac{16}{13})+(\frac{11}{13})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{3-5\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is $1+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{3-5\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{3-5\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-2\text{i}}{1-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{3-6\text{i}-5\text{i}+10{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3-11\text{i}+10(-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3-11\text{i}-10}{1+4} \\  & =\frac{-7-11\text{i}}{5}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: $\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}}=$
content.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-5+4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-5-4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-5-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}} & =\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-5-4\text{i}}{-5-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-45\text{i}-36{\text{i}}^{2}}{{5}^{2}-{4}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-45\text{i}-36(-1)}{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{36-45\text{i}}{25+16} \\  & =\frac{36-45\text{i}}{41}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{36-45\text{i}}{41}=\frac{36}{41}-\frac{45}{41}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: $\frac{15\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}=$
content.worked_solution:
The denominator is $1+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{15\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}} & =\frac{15\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-2\text{i}}{1-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{15\text{i}-30{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{15\text{i}-30(-1)}{1-4(-1)} \\  & =\frac{15\text{i}+30}{1+4} \\  & =\frac{30+15\text{i}}{5}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{30+15\text{i}}{5}=\frac{30}{5}+\frac{15}{5}\text{i}=6+3\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate -3-2i. The numerator becomes -27-18i and the denominator becomes 9+4=13. Thus the quotient is -27/13-(18/13)i, option a.

after.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-3+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-3-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{-3+2\text{i}} & =\frac{9}{-3+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-3-2\text{i}}{-3-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-27-18\text{i}}{9+6\text{i}-6\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-27-18\text{i}}{9-4(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-27-18\text{i}}{9+4} \\  & =\frac{-27-18\text{i}}{13}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-27-18\text{i}}{13}=-\frac{27}{13}-\frac{18}{13}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{1-12\text{i}}{8\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is the imaginary number $8\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+8\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-8\text{i},$ or simply $-8\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-8\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{1-12\text{i}}{8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{1-12\text{i}}{8\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-8\text{i}}{-8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-8\text{i}+96{\text{i}}^{2}}{-64{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-8\text{i}+96(-1)}{-64(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-96-8\text{i}}{64}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-96-8\text{i}}{64}=-\frac{96}{64}-\frac{8}{64}\text{i}=-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{8}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-4+9\text{i}}{6\text{i}} & =\frac{-4+9\text{i}}{6\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-6\text{i}}{-6\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{24\text{i}-54{\text{i}}^{2}}{-36{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{24\text{i}-54(-1)}{-36(-1)} \\  & =\frac{54+24\text{i}}{36}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{54+24\text{i}}{36} & =\frac{54}{36}+\frac{24}{36}\text{i} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2})+(\frac{2}{3})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
